physical_hbm_topology.admission_policy: FIFO and batch-class share one global admission clock; at most four 64-byte blocks enter all channel controllers per paper cycle, while each channel independently enforces the 32-entry read queue and 32-entry write buffer
physical_hbm_topology.command_queue_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini cmd_queue_size=8; the request-level controller bounds each bank command queue to the same depth
physical_hbm_topology.coordinator_input_policy: FIFO selects one Edge/Input/Weight/Output port per admission cycle, admits up to four consecutive blocks, and bounds the uncoordinated in-flight row windows to the four Figure 9 request sources; batch-class assembles batch-local Edge > Input > Weight > Output streams with same batch/class open-row continuation
physical_hbm_topology.coordinator_input_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Figure 9 shows four concurrent Edge, Input, Weight, and Output request sources; Section 4.5.2 says the uncoordinated requests are handled sequentially and the coordinator assembles them into continuous batch-local streams before low-bit remapping
physical_hbm_topology.coordinator_issue_width_source: derived from the paper profile peak interface width: floor(256 bytes/cycle divided by 64 bytes/block)

dram_timing.command_issue_interval_formula: ceil(tCK / model_cycle_ns); each physical channel issues row commands on its own replicated DRAMSim3 command lane
dram_timing.command_model: request completion is measured from actual READ/WRITE issue; row conflicts explicitly schedule PRE then ACT before the data command, while tWR/tRTP/tRAS and PRE-to-ACT constrain recovery
dram_timing.read_to_precharge_formula: ceil((AL + tRTP) * tCK / model_cycle_ns); bundled HBM config omits tRTP, so DRAMSim3 default tRTP=5 applies
dram_timing.read_to_write_formula: ceil((RL + burst_cycle - WL + tRTRS) * tCK / model_cycle_ns)
dram_timing.transfer_note: burst/block transfer is modeled separately by transfer_cycles, so BL is not duplicated in CL/CWL completion latency

physical_hbm_topology.low_bits_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Section 4.5.2: channel and bank identifiers use lower address bits

occupancy_trace.policy: every admission records per-channel read/write occupancy before and after mutation; a terminal zero snapshot lets the validator infer all intervening dispatch counts from zero and independently recompute peaks, capacity violations, totals, histograms, edge samples, and checksum

physical_hbm_topology.priority_order_source: HyGCN HPCA 2020 Section 4.5.2 executes requests batch-by-batch: all requests from the current batch, including its lower-priority classes, precede high-priority requests from the next batch
physical_hbm_topology.row_first_layout_basis: one row-sized block span stays in one bank, then the collapsed mapping advances channel and bank fields in the order represented by rorabgbachco
physical_hbm_topology.row_first_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini selects address_mapping=rorabgbachco. The collapsed request-level baseline therefore keeps every contiguous row span in one bank; it does not add an unsupported adjacent-bank striping factor.
physical_hbm_topology.topology_source: HyGCN reports 256 GB/s HBM1. The bundled DRAMSim3 HBM1_4Gb_x128 profile is one 8-channel 128 GB/s stack, so the paper profile replicates that timing and queue topology across two stacks rather than inventing a faster per-channel command rate.
physical_hbm_topology.transaction_queue_source: configs/HBM1_4Gb_x128.ini sets unified_queue=False and trans_queue_size=32; DRAMSim3 therefore allocates an independent 32-entry read_queue and 32-entry write_buffer in every channel controller
